rows.notes: The cited study is a narrative literature review (Section 3 describes a Web of Science/Scopus search and manual screening; Fig. 1 schematic of the review process; 'No data was used for the research'). It reports no experiment, survey, measurement or validated model of its own. Its statements that remote sensing optimises irrigation scheduling and conserves water (Section 3.1.1, Table 2) and its list of adoption barriers (Section 4.1) are syntheses of other work (Dari et al. 2020, Zhu et al. 2023, etc.), so none counts as the study's own result on the claim.

Same review; no primary data. Its discussion of IoT-based precision irrigation and smart-sensor scheduling platforms (Sections 3.1.3 and 3.1.6, Table 2) summarises cited studies (Monteleone et al. 2020, Khoa et al. 2019, Tzerakis et al. 2023, Manocha et al. 2024) rather than reporting any own test of app/IoT-based scheduling on water conservation. Barriers (cost, expertise, connectivity, cybersecurity) in Section 4.1 are also literature-derived.
